evidence: src/app/(app)/import/share/route.ts:39-41 says of the cross-site refusal: '(The session cookies are SameSite Lax, so a cross-site POST normally arrives without a session and the middleware has already sent it to sign-in; this check does not rely on that.)' delivery/work-history/m3-p5.yaml:92-95 says the same: 'the route's refusal stays its own rather than a property of a cookie attribute set elsewhere.'

At 98fbadc that is false for one request shape. src/app/(app)/import/share/route.ts:57-64: when Sec-Fetch-Site is absent and Origin is the literal null (or absent), isCrossSite returns false and the POST proceeds. A browser without Fetch Metadata (it is sent by Chromium and by current Firefox and Safari, but not by older Safari or Firefox) submitting a cross-site form from a sandboxed iframe, a data: URL or across a redirect sends exactly Origin: null with no Sec-Fetch-Site. For that shape the only thing between another site's page and the upload is the SameSite=Lax session cookie, which is the @supabase/ssr default (node_modules/@supabase/ssr/dist/main/utils/constants.js:6; nothing under src sets cookie options: grep -rn 'cookieOptions|sameSite' src finds only the comment).

Accepting Origin null is correct and required by the phase intent (the phone sends it); the fault is only the sentence claiming independence from the cookie attribute. Round one's route refused Origin null, so this dependence is new in the fix round and is not named anywhere.
findings.concrete-fix: Replace the last sentence of the comment at src/app/(app)/import/share/route.ts:39-41 and the matching sentence at delivery/work-history/m3-p5.yaml:92-95 with the true statement: where the browser sends Sec-Fetch-Site the route's refusal is its own; where it does not and the Origin is null or absent, the refusal rests on the session cookie being SameSite=Lax (the @supabase/ssr default), and the middleware then sends the POST to sign-in. Optionally pin that default with a unit assertion so a change to the cookie options is seen.
findings.analysis: R-087: a present-tense comment claim that nothing checks and that the fix round itself made untrue. No live exposure found: with Lax cookies the request reaches the middleware without a session and is answered 303 to sign-in, and a share target only exists on Chromium, which sends Fetch Metadata. Ranked low for that reason. ROUND 1 CRITERIA FINDINGS AT 98fbadc (recorded here because the verdict schema has no top-level analysis field; none of the three is re-raised). CR-M3P5-01 (medium): CLOSED. isCrossSite now refuses on Sec-Fetch-Site cross-site or same-site first (src/app/(app)/import/share/route.ts:54 and src/app/(app)/import/share/route.ts:57-60), treats Origin null like an absent Origin (src/app/(app)/import/share/route.ts:62-63), and keeps the host comparison for a parseable Origin (src/app/(app)/import/share/route.ts:65-66). Traced for the shipped Android Chrome share (Origin: null, Sec-Fetch-Site: none, session cookie attached): none is not in the refused set, null returns false, so the handler proceeds to requireHouseholdContext and uploadStatement. Unit case test/app/share-route.test.ts:110-116 asserts 303 and one upload; scratchpad route-red.txt shows it failing against the round one route (expected 403 to be 303, 1 failed 12 passed) and my run at 98fbadc passes it (npm test exit 0, 778 of 778). The e2e share at test/e2e/share-target.spec.ts:153-163 now sends origin null and sec-fetch-site none through the real middleware and route and passed under chromium and chromium-phone at the fix head (e2e-p5-fr1.txt:333 and e2e-p5-fr1.txt:699). The refusal side: test/app/share-route.test.ts:118-128 (Sec-Fetch-Site cross-site and same-site with Origin null, 403 before the context is read) and :100-105 (foreign Origin); the e2e cross-site case test/e2e/share-target.spec.ts:99-112 passed at e2e-p5-fr1.txt:332 and :698. The comment at src/app/(app)/import/share/route.ts:28-41 is corrected, and the on-device headers are recorded as owed evidence (delivery/work-history/m3-p5.yaml:204-207 and claim C-5-on-device at delivery/work-history/m3-p5.yaml:308-317). CR-M3P5-02 (low): CLOSED. src/app/manifest.ts:19-23 now states the no-service-worker installability as Chromium's documented behaviour, not measured, and points at owed evidence; delivery/work-history/m3-p5.yaml:113-117 says the same and C-5-on-device is an open claim. No source is cited in the comment, but I checked it: web.dev/articles/install-criteria (fetched in this review, HTTP 200) lists name or short_name, 192 and 512 icons, start_url, display and prefer_related_applications, and no service worker, so the recast statement is true. CR-M3P5-03 (low): CLOSED. test/e2e/share-target.spec.ts:141-144 opens /?month=2026-05 after the first share's confirm and asserts recon-panel data-state ok, the same month and assertion test/e2e/import.spec.ts:205 uses for criterion 2.5; passed at e2e-p5-fr1.txt:333 and e2e-p5-fr1.txt:699. PHASE INTENT AT 98fbadc: delivered, as far as a container can show. A real share from shipped Android Chrome (Origin: null, Sec-Fetch-Site: none, as the round one hazard verdict established from Chromium source) passes src/app/(app)/import/share/route.ts:57-64 and reaches the upload; witnessed by the unit case test/app/share-route.test.ts:110-116 (red against the round one route in route-red.txt) and by the e2e share at test/e2e/share-target.spec.ts:153-163 through the real middleware and route. The future Chromium shape (Origin: this site, Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin) passes the host comparison at src/app/(app)/import/share/route.ts:66, as test/app/share-route.test.ts:136-140 shows for the Origin half. A genuine cross-site POST from a modern browser carries Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site and is refused 403 before the session or body is read (src/app/(app)/import/share/route.ts:58-59, test/app/share-route.test.ts:118-128); with a foreign URL Origin it is refused by the host check (test/app/share-route.test.ts:100-105, e2e test/e2e/share-target.spec.ts:99-112 with a session present); and without a session it never reaches the route (src/middleware.ts:51-54). WHAT THIS CONTRACT DID NOT REACH: no Android device, so the headers a real share carries and the installability of the manifest are not witnessed (owed, claim C-5-on-device); the share tests run on the dev server only (the prod project's testMatch at playwright.config.ts:84 and :158 does not include share-target), so the route under next start with Origin null is unwitnessed; the e2e log carries no sha and was attributed to 31fd73d by timing; I did not run Playwright or start a server, so the curl half of 5.1 is a substitution; the hazard lane's own findings (HZ-002 body size, left open as claim C-5-body-size; HZ-005's requested matcher unit test, not added) are the hazard lane's to judge, and I checked only that the anchored matcher behaves as its comment says (path-to-regexp probe: /manifest.webmanifest excluded; /manifest.webmanifest/x, /manifestXwebmanifest and /import/share run the middleware). All criteria met is one input here, not a completeness claim.
